ar_sloping_joe_boulder.blurb: Sloping Joe Boulder is a small bouldering spot on the east side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, in the sandstone of north-central Arkansas. It holds eleven problems from VB-level warm-ups up to V6, though most of them sit at the easier end, with a few in the V3 to V5 range and one hard line at the top. As the name hints, the rock here is known for slopers, so it works well as a warm-up before heading to the steeper boulders nearby. It is one stop in a spread-out bouldering zone, not a destination on its own, so plan to link it with neighbouring blocks.

ar_prophecy_wall.blurb: Prophecy Wall is a steep, overhanging sport wall on the west side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, set in the fine sandstone of the Arkansas Ozarks. It has eleven bolted lines spanning a wide range: one easy route in the 5.7 to 5.8 bracket, a couple of 5.10s, a solid cluster of 5.11s, and a handful of hard lines from 5.12 up to the low 5.14s. Expect sustained, pumpy climbing on an overhanging face, which makes it better suited to strong leaders than to people building up from beginner grades. The approach is a short hike from the meadow, crossing a seasonal creek on the way.

ar_boneyard_the.blurb: The Boneyard is a compact cluster of boulders at Bigfoot Hollow in the eastern Boston Mountains of Arkansas, roughly an hour from Fayetteville. It is the first bouldering zone you meet along the road in, with blocks scattered down toward the gully beside the main campground. The eleven problems run from V0 to V7: a few easy warm-ups, a middle band around V2 and V3, and a harder top end of V5 to V7. The boulders mostly face south, and the first problem is only a short walk from where you park. It is a good quick stop rather than a full-day venue.

ar_atlantis.blurb: Atlantis is a small bouldering area right on the edge of Lake Lincoln in northwest Arkansas. It stays shady all year and can be very cold in winter, and because it sits at the water's edge it occasionally floods. The eleven problems are mostly in the V3 to V5 range, with a few harder lines up to V8 and one very hard problem around V11. Standouts include a big roof crack and a compression problem that is one of the area's best-known lines. Expect an adventurous walk-in that finishes with a short downclimb to reach the first boulders.
